rv.q: Those cheap tickets buy you not only a seat at the Minetta Lane but also a place in the living conversation of raw yet thoughtful theater.
And the play, by the Canadian writer Hannah Moscovitch, provides Mr. Jackman with a snug showcase for his admirable ability to give audiences a big bear hug without leaving the stage.
Smartly written and exceedingly well-acted, Sexual Misconduct proves just how seductive the author’s voice can be.
It’s a terrific role for him: a self-deprecating, self-aware prof who admits he tries—perhaps too hard—to adopt a “casual, jokey style” in his lectures.

Despite its title, I’m not convinced Moscovitch has much to say about the “middle class” or its specific morality, but she has definitely provided audiences with a more than middlebrow play and an above-average vehicle for two very talented actors.
The actor doesn’t disappoint, showcasing his character’s vulnerabilities, self-doubt and even pettiness when he finds the tables turned on him late in the story.
And yet, I'm glad to have seen it. A main reason is Jackman's performance in the relatively intimate space of the Theater; he was indeed engaging.
Sexual Misconduct of the Middle Classes is clever in its casting and narrative style, but at the same time, the text is written like a syllabus, right down to the academic title.
In fact, it’s one of the most gripping and entertaining dramas of the year.
This play is a powerful voice uplifting the lessons of college—not in school, but in life.
It is an intriguing and thought-provoking adult fairy tale with a marvelous final twist and purposely ambiguous moral.

cn.t: Critics praise Jackman's charismatic, seductive performance in Moscovitch's absorbing two-hander, which skillfully frames a provocative professor-student affair through compelling theatrical storytelling and sharp direction.

vr.q: When you can cut that type of engaged energy with a knife, you know it's good theatre.
I thoroughly enjoyed it despite these minor criticisms, and for a ticket price of $30, I think it's well worth the time.
